punchline: 168 Spaniards took an emperor at Cajamarca, and Diamond says the answer is not courage but what each side started with.
thirty_sec: In 1532 Pizarro met the Inca emperor at Cajamarca with 168 men. They had horses, steel and guns, and the Inca army of tens of thousands had none of them. They captured Atahualpa the same day. Jared Diamond explains it with starting conditions, and smallpox had already hit the Inca before the Spanish arrived.
